analysis: Docs-only change to docs/architecture/inference.md. Head lines 25-171 add a Nemotron Super local-owner description: an unregistered NemotronSuperLocalBridgeBuilder, a load transaction, image/text bindings, an optional authenticated loopback HTTP hook (`NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP`, absent by default, no production caller), a resident prefix-checkpoint bank gated by DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1 using the local unscoped cache scope, and an opt-in MTP mode (DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP=1). A smaller edit at head 876-877 aligns the vision_config template check with the shared media discovery policy. No code, endpoint, or deployment changes; the described paths are explicitly unregistered. The doc states bounded ingress/media charges and memory reservations, media-decode limits, a 429 on queueFull, and rejection of tools, media, and client prompt-cache keys on the text binding. The only gap I found is that T-041 asserts there is no resident-RAM production prefix cache, which would not hold if this owner were wired into production (flagged as a low finding). Later reviewers should check the underlying Swift sources, which were not supplied, for the cache scope, the HTTP hook's authentication, and the image decode bounds. The doc's claims about these are unverified.

findings.detail: The new documentation describes `NemotronSuperLocalPrefixCache`, which gives the plain owner a resident recurrent checkpoint bank when `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1`, and says text requests use 'the local unscoped cache scope'. T-041 states that production never constructs or funds a resident-RAM prefix cache, and that the single `DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE` gate controls an encrypted SSD tier whose scope is coordinator-authored per account. The new bank is a separate env gate, resident in RAM, unencrypted, and not scoped by account. The doc says the paths are unregistered and not exposed over HTTP, and that no production caller installs the hook, so this is not an active regression. If the owner is later wired to production, it would reintroduce a cross-tenant sharing and TTFT oracle that T-041 and SEC-035 treat as closed or narrowed. T-041 should be updated to say this bank is out of production scope, or to cover it, before any wiring. Add a note requiring cacheScope plumbing and a fresh SEC-035 sign-off.
findings.title: Threat model does not cover new Nemotron Super local prefix-cache bank (resident RAM tier, local unscoped cache scope)
